 Audi Recalls More Than 9,000 Electric Vehicles Over Fire Risk — Owners Told to Limit Charging
 Daniel Webster 2026년 10월 26일 월 오전 10:20 UTC 0 Audi is recalling 9,048 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron electric vehicles from the 2024 and 2025 model years due to a potential high-voltage battery fire risk. Affected owners are advised to limit charging to 80% until repairs are available. VanderWolf Images/Shutterstock Volkswagen Group of America is recalling 9,048 Audi electric vehicles because their high-voltage batteries may fail and potentially cause a fire. Owners of affected vehicles are being advised to limit charging to 80% battery capacity while the manufacturer develops a permanent repair.
 According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) , the recall covers certain 2024 and 2025 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles. The safety action was reported to federal regulators on October 21, 2026, under NHTSA campaign number 26V698000.
 The agency warns that a vehicle fire increases the risk of injury. Because the permanent remedy remains under development, affected owners should follow Audi’s interim charging instructions rather than waiting for an official notification letter.
 Which Audi Electric Vehicles Are Being Recalled?
 The recall affects certain vehicles from the following model years:
 2024 Audi Q4 E-Tron
 2025 Audi Q4 E-Tron
 2024 Audi Q4 Sportback E-Tron
 2025 Audi Q4 Sportback E-Tron
 A total of 9,048 vehicles are potentially affected nationwide.
 The problem involves the high-voltage battery system, which stores the electricity used to power the vehicle. According to the federal recall information, the battery may fail and create a fire hazard.
 NHTSA has not identified every vehicle from these model years as defective. Owners must check their individual Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) to determine whether their vehicle is included.
 Owners Are Being Told to Limit Battery Charging
 Audi’s immediate recommendation is to charge affected vehicles to no more than 80% of their battery capacity until the necessary repair has been completed.
 For drivers accustomed to charging their vehicles to 100% before longer trips, this restriction could require adjustments to their usual driving and charging routines.
 The charging limitation is intended to reduce potential safety risks while engineers develop a permanent solution.
 Importantly, the official recall summary does not instruct owners to stop driving their vehicles or park them outdoors. Owners should follow the specific guidance associated with this recall rather than assuming precautions issued for other electric vehicle recalls also apply here.
 Anyone who notices unusual battery behavior or receives additional warnings should contact an authorized Audi dealership for guidance.
 When Will Audi Notify Owners?
 Audi expects to begin mailing interim notification letters on December 18, 2026.
 These letters will inform owners about the safety risk and the temporary precautions they should follow.
 Because a permanent repair is still being developed, owners will receive additional notification once the remedy becomes available.
 Federal safety recalls generally require manufacturers to provide the necessary repairs at no cost to vehicle owners. The NHTSA recall program provides information about recall responsibilities and how consumers can obtain repairs.
 Audi’s internal recall reference number is 93SK.
 How to Check Whether Your Audi Is Affected
 Owners do not need to wait until December to determine whether their vehicles are included.
 Advertisement
 NHTSA reports that affected VINs became searchable through its official recall database on October 23, 2026.
 Drivers can visit NHTSA.gov/recalls and enter their 17-character VIN to check for outstanding safety recalls.
 The VIN is typically located on the driver’s side of the dashboard near the windshield or on the driver’s door jamb.
 Owners can also contact Audi customer service at 1-800-253-2834 and reference recall number 93SK.
 Because recall information can change as repairs become available, checking the official database periodically can help owners stay informed.
 What This Recall Could Mean for Owners
 Beyond the immediate safety concern, the charging restriction may create practical inconveniences for drivers who rely on their electric vehicles for daily transportation.
 Limiting charging to 80% reduces the amount of battery capacity available for a trip compared with a full charge. Depending on driving conditions and charging access, some owners may need to stop more frequently during longer journeys.
 That could create additional planning challenges for people who regularly commute long distances or travel through areas with limited charging infrastructure.
 However, the recall does not establish that affected vehicles will necessarily experience battery failure, nor does it provide evidence that the defect has reduced their resale value.
 Owners concerned about repair scheduling, charging restrictions, or other vehicle-related expenses should contact Audi directly for information specific to their situation.
 Don’t Wait for the Recall Letter to Check Your Vehicle
 The Audi Q4 E-Tron recall highlights why vehicle owners should regularly check for safety notices, particularly when manufacturers are still developing repairs.
 With more than 9,000 electric vehicles potentially affected, owners of 2024 and 2025 Q4 E-Tron models should verify their recall status as soon as possible.
 Those whose vehicles are included should follow the temporary 80% charging limit and watch for further instructions from Audi.
 The most reliable sources for updated information are the NHTSA recall database , Audi’s authorized dealerships, and the manufacturer’s customer service department.
 Have you experienced an electric vehicle recall that required changing your driving or charging habits? Share your experience in the comments.
